newsitem.title: UK: UK minister resisting air traffic sell-off - FT.
newsitem.headline: UK minister resisting air traffic sell-off - FT.

text.p: The UK transport minister Sir George Young has warned that a Treasury proposal to revive plans to privatise the air traffic control service before the general election would be controversial and complicated, the Financial Times newspaper said in its Thursday edition.
The paper said Young believed the privatisation might also prove hard to push through parliament in the remaining months before an election, which must be called by May 1997.

It said chancellor Kenneth Clarke is looking at ways of raising revenue ahead of the budget and sees the sale of National Air Traffic Services, which is a subsidiary of the Civil Aviation Authority, as raising at least 600 million stg.
The sale of the air traffic control service was dropped last year in the face of opposition from airlines and members of parliament on the transport select committee.
